# Google Workspace Adds Timed Pauses and Faster File Labels

> **In short:** Google says Workspace Studio flows can now pause for up to 14 days and restart automatically. In Drive, Docs, Sheets and Slides, one click on Accept now confirms a single automatic file label. Rollouts start November 9, 2026.

Have you ever wanted an email to go out on Monday morning, not Friday night? Or wished a file did not need extra clicks just to mark it correctly? Google's two newest Workspace updates target both of those small annoyances.

## Pausing a workflow with "Wait until"

Google Workspace Studio lets you build a **flow**, which is an automated sequence of steps that runs when something triggers it. Think of it as a set of instructions a computer follows on your behalf, like "when this happens, send that."

Until now, a flow with a built-in delay had to be split into several separate flows. Google's new **"Wait until" step** removes that workaround. You can place it at any point in a flow, including inside a **Check if** branch (a path that runs only when a condition is true) or a **Repeat for each** loop (a step that runs once per item in a list).

You have three ways to set the pause:

- **Specific day next week:** the flow continues on the next Monday at a time you choose. This suits non-urgent notifications.
- **Specific day and time:** for example, three days later at 5 p.m. This works well for follow-up emails and deadline reminders.
- **After a set duration:** a pause of minutes, hours, seconds, or a combination, up to 14 days in total.

You can watch a paused flow in the Activity tab of Workspace Studio. Google says it logs the scheduled restart time and time zone, so you can confirm that a flow is waiting as planned.

💬 *Example you might build:* a flow that sends a thank-you email right after a client meeting, then a follow-up three days later.

## Confirming file labels in one click

Google Workspace can apply **classification labels** to files. A label is a tag that describes how sensitive or important a file is, such as "internal only." Labels can be applied in two automatic ways: through **default classification** (rules set in advance) or through **AI classification** (where the system suggests a label based on the content).

Previously, an automatically labeled file showed only a Review button in the top banner. Now, when exactly one label is applied and you have permission to change it, the banner offers two buttons:

- **Accept** confirms the label in a single click.
- **Edit** opens the Labels side panel so you can change it.

If several labels are applied at once, the banner still shows Review, and you check them in the side panel. Google says the change is meant to reduce extra steps and keep label records accurate across an organization.

## Who gets these updates, and when

For the Wait until step, Google lists availability for Business Starter, Standard, and Plus; Enterprise Standard and Plus; and several Education editions and add-ons. The label update covers a wider list of editions, including Business Standard and Plus, and Enterprise Starter, Standard, and Plus. Check the official Help Center for your exact edition, because the lists differ.

Admins do not need to switch anything on for Wait until. For the label feature, Google says it will be on by default for organizations using default classification or AI classification with Drive labels. Rollouts start November 9, 2026. Wait until is expected to appear within 1 to 3 days, and the label change within up to 15 days.

## What this means for you

- **If you manage a team's routine work:** a single flow can now handle a multi-day sequence, so you no longer need to track several separate schedules.
- **If you handle client or company files:** the Accept button gives you a faster way to confirm a correct label. Still look at each label before you accept it.
- **If you are just getting started:** start with one simple flow and one delay. Test it with a message to yourself before you rely on it.
- **If you already use it:** combine a Wait until step inside a Repeat for each loop, so every item in a list gets its own timed follow-up.

## Wrap-up

Google's two updates help you control when automated work happens and make file labeling less of a chore. Check whether your Workspace edition is on the official list, then open Workspace Studio when the feature reaches your account and try a single delayed step. Start small, and you will see how much smoother the process feels.
